info.title: Delhivery Maps API
info.description:
Public API documentation for the Delhivery Maps Gateway.

All requests must be routed through this gateway.

## Authentication

All endpoints require a Bearer JWT in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-jwt-token>
```

The token must carry a `data.ucid` claim used for rate limiting and traceability.

| Scenario | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Missing/malformed header | `401 { "detail": "Missing or invalid Authorization header" }` |
| Expired token | `401 { "detail": "Token has expired" }` |
| Invalid token | `401 { "detail": "Invalid token" }` |

## Rate Limiting

Requests are rate-limited per user (50 requests / 24 hours). Response headers:

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Max requests in the window |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix epoch when the window resets |

When exhausted: `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` header.

## Coverage

All coordinate-based endpoints operate within India only.

post.description:
Calculates the optimal route between 2+ waypoints within India.
Supports multiple travel modes, alternate routes, and route modifiers.

**BREAKING CHANGE (v4.7):** Geometry is now **encoded** by default. Unless you send `output_format: { "encode_polyline": false }`, both `geometry` and every `legs[].shape` are returned as encoded polyline strings (precision 6). Maneuvers are **off** by default — send `output_format: { "maneuvers": true }` to include them. The old `decode_geometry` query parameter has been removed; use `output_format.encode_polyline` in the request body instead.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Travel Mode | Max Locations |
| --- | --- |
| auto | 20 |
| motorcycle | 50 |
| truck | 20 |
| pedestrian | 50 |

Requests exceeding the max location count return HTTP 400. There is no pre-check for maximum distance.

post.summary: Verify delivery history at an address
post.description:
Checks whether a confirmed delivery has reached a specific address within the last N months. Address validation runs first — the history lookup only proceeds on a valid, premise-level match.

`is_verified=false` can mean: address could not be resolved, no delivery recorded in the window, address not specific enough (PREMISE level required), or no delivery records found at this location.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Parameter | Range |
| --- | --- |
| `months` min | 1 |
| `months` max | 24 |

post.description:
Returns a GeoJSON polygon covering everywhere reachable from an origin within a single cost budget.

One endpoint serves both products — the `cost_type` field in the body selects which:

| Cost Type | Product | Cost Value Unit | Question answered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | IsoChrone | seconds | "How far can I get in 10 minutes?" |
| `distance` | IsoDistance | metres | "How far can I get within 5 km of road travel?" |

Everything else — request shape, validation, response shape, error codes — is identical between the two modes. The response echoes the mode back in `features[0].properties.cost_type`.

`direction` flips the direction of travel: `outbound` (default) is where you can reach from the origin; `inbound` is who can reach the origin. The two differ on one-ways, restricted turns and time-dependent costing.

Exactly one contour is requested per call, so the response always contains exactly one feature.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Cost Type | Unit | Min (exclusive) | Max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | seconds | 0 | 7,200 |
| `distance` | metres | 0 | 100,000 |

| Travel Mode | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| auto | Yes |
| motorcycle | Yes |
| truck | Yes |
| pedestrian | Yes |

`cost_value` must satisfy `0 < cost_value <= max`. A value of `0`, a negative value, or a value above the max returns HTTP 400. A larger `cost_value` explores a larger area and costs more latency; the max caps worst-case compute time.

The origin must lie inside the India boundary.

**RESPONSE GEOMETRY FORMAT**

By default, or when `encode_geojson` is omitted, the response uses encoded polyline strings to reduce response size. If you want standard GeoJSON coordinates directly, send `encode_geojson: false`.

| `encode_geojson` | Response geometry |
| --- | --- |
| omitted or `true` (default) | Encoded polyline strings |
| `false` | Standard GeoJSON numeric coordinate arrays in `[longitude, latitude]` order |

Optional `latitude ` and `longitude` bias ranking toward the user's location.

- Lat/Long pair → returns a single synthetic coordinate result

post.summary: Estimate toll charges between an origin-destination pair
post.description:
Calculates toll charges for a journey between an origin and destination coordinate pair.
The system computes the route internally and identifies toll plazas along the route.
Supports multiple vehicle types and optionally returns alternate routes with their toll breakdowns.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Constraint | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Waypoints | Optional ordered intermediate stops between origin & destination |
| Vehicle types | `motorcycle`, `car_jeep_van`, `lcv`, `bus_truck`, `upto_3_axle`, `axle_4_to_6`, `hcm_eme`, `axle_7_plus` |
| Max routes returned | 1 recommended + alternates |

> When `waypoints` are supplied, the routing engine returns a single stitched route (no alternates), regardless of `include_alternates`.

post.summary: Estimate toll charges along user-provided route polylines.
post.description:
Calculates toll charges for one or more route polylines provided by the user.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Constraint | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Max polylines per request | 3 |

| Minimum Polyline Coordinates | 2 coordinate pairs per route |
| Polyline format | Array of `[lat, lon]` pairs |
| Vehicle types | `motorcycle`, `car_jeep_van`, `lcv`, `bus_truck`, `upto_3_axle`, `axle_4_to_6`, `hcm_eme`, `axle_7_plus` |

post.summary: Calculate optimized, capacity-aware delivery routes across a multi-vehicle fleet to minimize total distance, transit time, and operational costs.
post.description:
Solves the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) by assigning delivery orders across a fleet of vehicles from a central depot to generate optimized, stop-by-stop routes.

Accepts location data as exact coordinates or text addresses with automatic geocoding. The engine minimizes total transit distance and duration while enforcing per-vehicle weight and volume limits.

**ORDER LOCATION**

Each order must specify either a order coordinate pair (`lat, long`) or an order address. If an address is provided, it is automatically geocoded, and the resolved coordinates are returned in the resulting route stop payload.

**SERVICE LIMITS**

| Constraint | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Orders | Must be between 1 and 50. |
| Order Address | Order address must be located in India. |
| Order Location | Order Location must be within Indian territory. |

orders.description: A list of dictionaries where each dictionary contains the metadata of an order.

num_vehicles.description: Number of vehicles available at the depot.

vehicle_max_weight.description: Maximum weight in kilograms that one vehicle in this contract can serve. Defaults to 1000 kg.

vehicle_max_volume.description: Maximum volume in cubic centimeters that one vehicle in this contract can serve. Defaults to 100000 cm³.

max_stops.description: Maximum number of unique locations a vehicle can visit in a route apart from its starting location. Defaults to 100.

max_distance.description: Maximum distance in kilometers till which the vehicle can be used. Defaults to 1000 km.

max_time.description: Maximum time in seconds till which the vehicle can be used. Defaults to 86400 seconds (1 day).

plan_start_time.description: Absolute wall-clock time at which the vehicle shift begins (e.g., '2026-06-03 09:00+05:30'). If missing, order time windows are dropped.

return_to_depot.description: Controls whether vehicles must return to the depot after serving their last order.

vehicle_mode.description: Travel mode passed through to the distance-matrix API. Allowed values: 'auto', 'truck', 'bike', 'foot'.

PlanOrder.description: A single order. Provide either order_lat/order_lng or order_address.

order_address.description: Complete delivery address of the order. Either order_address or (order_lat, order_lng) must be provided.

order_lat.description: Order latitude. Required if order_address is not provided.

order_lng.description: Order longitude. Required if order_address is not provided.

order_service_duration.description: Total time in seconds to service the demand of this order once a vehicle has arrived at the location. Defaults to 0 seconds.

order_weight.description: Total weight in kilograms of all items in the order. Defaults to 0 kg.

order_volume.description: Total volume in cubic centimeters of all items in the order. Defaults to 0 cm³.

order_time_window_start.description: Earliest time a vehicle can serve the order in format 'yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm' (e.g., '2024-06-17 14:30').

order_time_window_end.description: Latest time till which a vehicle can serve the order in format 'yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm' (e.g., '2024-06-17 23:30').

plan_status.description: True if the solver found a solution, else False.

routes_info.description: List of routes generated by the solver, containing vehicle details, order assignments, route sequence, and metrics.

unassigned_orders.description: List of order IDs that could not be assigned to any vehicle by the solver.

PlanSummary.description: Summary dictionary of the overall CVRP solution generated by the solver.

total_orders.description: Total number of orders provided in the input payload.

assigned_orders.description: Total number of orders successfully assigned to vehicles in the solution.

unassigned_orders.description: Total number of orders that could not be assigned to any vehicle in the solution.

vehicles_used.description: Total number of vehicles used in the solution.

total_distance.description: Total distance travelled by all vehicles across all routes in the solution.

total_duration.description: Total duration of all routes in the solution in seconds.

vehicle_id.description: Unique identifier of the vehicle assigned to the route.

orders.description: Ordered list of order IDs assigned to the vehicle for the route.

route.description: Ordered sequence of locations visited by the vehicle.

total_distance.description: Total distance travelled by the vehicle for the route in kilometers.

total_duration.description: Total duration of the route in seconds, including travel and service time.

total_weight.description: Total weight in kilograms of all orders assigned to the vehicle for the route.

total_volume.description: Total volume in cubic centimeters of all orders assigned to the vehicle for the route.

num_stops.description: Total number of order stops visited by the vehicle in the route.

type.description: Type of location in the route ('depot' or 'order').

order_id.description: Unique identifier of the order being serviced (applicable when type is 'order').

sequence.description: Sequence number of the order stop in the route.

geo_coords.description: Ordered `[lat, lng]` waypoints. Minimum 2, all within India.

travel_mode.description: One of auto, motorcycle, truck, pedestrian.

departure_time.description: Specifies the planned departure time (for example, `2026-06-03T18:00`) in ISO-8601 format. Defaults to the current time. This parameter is considered only when `traffic_aware` is set to `true`.

output_format.description: Controls how the response is shaped. Both keys are optional and default-merged, so you may send just one.

encode_polyline.description: `true` → `geometry` and each `legs[].shape` are encoded polyline strings (precision 6). `false` → both are decoded `[[lat, lng], ...]` point lists. Replaces the old `decode_geometry` query parameter.

maneuvers.description: `false` → the `maneuvers` key is absent from every leg. `true` → each leg includes a `maneuvers` array (with `bearing_after`, `bearing_before`, `cost`, `travel_type`, `travel_mode`, and `time` removed from each maneuver).

geometry.description: Encoded polyline string (precision 6) when `output_format.encode_polyline` is `true` (default), else decoded `[[lat, lng], ...]`.

snap_distance_m.description: Distance in meters from the input coordinate to the snapped road point.

shape.description: Encoded polyline for the leg (precision 6) when `output_format.encode_polyline` is `true`, else decoded `[[lat, lng], ...]`.

maneuvers.description: Present only when `output_format.maneuvers` is `true`. Each maneuver excludes `bearing_after`, `bearing_before`, `cost`, `travel_type`, `travel_mode`, and `time`.

alternates.description: Alternate routes (same structure as `recommended_route`). Empty array if none.

sources.description: List of `[lat, lng]` source coordinates. All within India.

targets.description: List of `[lat, lng]` target coordinates. All within India.

error_radius.description: Positional uncertainty in meters. Lower = higher confidence.

pincode.description: Postal code of the geocoded location.

origin.description: Origin point as `[latitude, longitude]`. Must be inside India.

cost_type.description: Selects the product: `time` → isochrone (budget in seconds), `distance` → isodistance (budget in metres).

cost_value.description: The budget. Seconds when `cost_type` is `time` (max 7,200 = 120 min); metres when `cost_type` is `distance` (max 100,000 = 100 km). Must be greater than 0.

travel_mode.description: Vehicle profile used for the expansion.

direction.description: `outbound` = area reachable from the origin; `inbound` = area that can reach the origin.

resolution.description: Polygon detail. `high` returns more vertices and a tighter boundary at a small latency cost; `low` returns a coarser, lighter polygon.

enable_smoothing.description: Reserved. Accepted and type-validated, but currently has no effect on the returned geometry.

departure_time.description: Departure time in IST, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. Only used when `traffic_aware` is `true`.

encode_geojson.description: Response geometry format. The default is `true` when this field is omitted, which returns encoded geometry to reduce response size. Set to `false` to receive standard GeoJSON numeric coordinate arrays in `[longitude, latitude]` order. This changes only the response representation, not the computed reachable area.

req_id.description: Optional client correlation id — echoed back in the response and recorded in logs.

IsochroneRouteModifiers.description: Road-class preferences applied to the expansion.

IsochroneResponse.description: A GeoJSON `FeatureCollection` with two extra top-level keys (`status`, `request_id`) that do not affect GeoJSON compatibility. Always contains exactly one feature.

features.description: Exactly one feature — one contour is requested per call.

req_id.description: Echoed from the request. Present only if the client sent it.

request_id.description: Server-generated id for log tracing. Quote this when reporting an issue.

cost_type.description: Echo of the request — tells you whether this polygon is an isochrone or an isodistance.

cost_value.description: Echo of the request budget (seconds for `time`, metres for `distance`).

travel_mode.description: Echo of the resolved travel mode (`auto` when the request omitted it).

area_sq_km.description: Area enclosed by the polygon in square kilometres, rounded to 2 decimal places.

IsochronePolygon.description: Reachable-area geometry returned by the Isochrone/Isodistance API. By default, or when `encode_geojson` is omitted, the geometry is returned in an encoded format to reduce response size. To receive standard GeoJSON coordinates directly, send `encode_geojson: false`. With `encode_geojson: false`, coordinates are numeric GeoJSON arrays in `[longitude, latitude]` order. The request `origin` uses `[latitude, longitude]` order.

coordinates.description: Response coordinates depend on `encode_geojson`. By default, or when omitted, the API returns encoded geometry to reduce response size. Set `encode_geojson: false` to receive standard GeoJSON numeric coordinate arrays directly in `[longitude, latitude]` order. The default encoded form and the standard GeoJSON form represent the same area.

error_code.description: Present on routing-engine errors only. `1001` = type error, `1002` = value error, `1003` = routing/upstream error. Absent on API-level errors (missing payload, missing field, invalid travel mode).

req_id.description: Echoed from the request. Present only if the client sent it.

address_text.description: Raw input address string. It should not be blank.

latitude.description: Latitude of the visit / attempt location. It should be within the Indian subcontinent.

longitude.description: Longitude of the visit / attempt location. It should be within the Indian subcontinent.

radius_meters.description: Target radius in meters, 10 to 1000 (both inclusive). Defaults to the service's configured default radius when omitted; values outside the range return 422.

is_within_target_radius.description: True when the visit location matches a known address cluster within the target radius.

granularity_level.description: Finest verified semantic level; null when no match.

estimated_distance_meters.description: Estimated distance in meters between the visit location and the matched address; null when no match.

req_id.description: Optional request id for tracing. If provided it must be non-empty; if omitted, the service auto-generates a UUID and returns it in the response.

waypoints.description: Optional ordered list of intermediate stops between origin and destination. The route visits them in order. When supplied, a single stitched route is returned (no alternates).

vehicle_type.description: Vehicle category for toll rate lookup.

include_alternates.description: If true, returns toll breakdowns for alternate routes in addition to the recommended route. Ignored when waypoints are supplied.

include_polyline.description: If true, each route in the response includes a `polyline` field with the ordered `[lat, lon]` route geometry.

req_id.description: Optional request id for tracing. If provided it must be non-empty; if omitted, the service auto-generates a UUID and returns it in the response.

routes.description: Array of route objects with user-provided geometry.

route_name.description: Optional human-readable label for the route. Defaults to `Route N`.

geometry.description: Ordered array of `[lat, lon]` coordinate pairs defining the route.

vehicle_type.description: Vehicle category for toll rate lookup.

TollRouteResult.description: Toll breakdown for a single route.

route_name.description: Label for the route (e.g. 'Recommended Route', 'Alternate 1', or user-provided name).

route_type.description: Whether this is the recommended or an alternate route. Only present in by-od responses.

distance_km.description: Total route distance in kilometres. Only present in by-od responses.

duration_sec.description: Estimated travel time in seconds. Only present in by-od responses.

polyline.description: Ordered `[lat, lon]` pairs of the full route geometry. Only present in by-od responses when `include_polyline` is true.

states_entered.description: States crossed during the journey (excluding origin state), in traversal order.

sequence_no.description: 1-indexed order in which the state is entered.

toll_plaza_count.description: Number of toll items on this route (a close_loop pair counts as one).

total_toll_inr.description: Sum of all toll plaza charges in INR.

total_cost_inr.description: Total journey cost in INR. Equal to total_toll_inr.

toll_plazas.description: Ordered list of toll plazas encountered, in travel direction. Items are either flat tolls or close-loop tolls.

CloseLoopTollPlaza.description: A closed-loop (entry/exit) toll where the charge depends on distance travelled between two plazas.

toll_rate_inr.description: Computed toll charge in INR based on entry-to-exit distance.

bearerAuth.description: Delhivery Maps JWT. Send as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
